title: Municipal councillors’ sit-in outside the Primature over pay, elections and working arrangements
location: Outside the Primature, Kinshasa; participants came from different provinces
organizer: Elected municipal councillors from several provinces
summary: Radio Okapi confirms the sit-in continued for more than four days as of 14 Dec and reports state-directed claims, but no turnout. The exact start date is inferred from “more than four days” and Dec 10 notices; continuity with earlier city-hall actions is unproven.

occurrence.evidence: Observed sit-in outside Primature continuing as of 14 Dec.

date.evidence: More than four days as of 14 Dec suggests onset before/around 10 Dec; exact onset uncertain.

location.evidence: Kinshasa Primature; participants came from different provinces, not necessarily multiple protest sites.

demand.evidence: Government support, elections of bourgmestres, and working arrangements with appointed mayors.

state_target.evidence: Claimants addressed the Prime Minister’s office/Government.

attendance_simultaneous.evidence: No headcount; different-province origins are not a count.

notes: A second-day meeting with cabinet staff and protocol proposal were described, but no signature or policy response had occurred by the article date. A search-only ACP result may describe a prior Oct city-hall wage action, but does not establish same episode; do not merge.
open_questions: How many councillors participated simultaneously in the Primature sit-in, and what evidence narrows its early-December onset?
Do the search-only reports of earlier city-hall wage claims document the same organizers or a continuous episode?

title: ANADEC employees’ multi-site road blocks and protests over wage arrears
location: Multiple sites in DRC: CongoRassure names Lubumbashi and the provinces North Kivu, Maniema and Kongo-Central; some precise city locations are unclear
organizer: ANADEC public-agency employees / intersyndicale not individually identified
summary: CongoRassure reports a coordinated multi-site action from 04:00 on 30 Dec with road blockages and closed offices over 13 months of arrears and an unimplemented agreement with the supervising minister/agency board. Attendance per site is unreported and not aggregated.

occurrence.evidence: Body reports mobilization and blockages from 04:00 on 30 Dec.

location.evidence: Several locations; source names Lubumbashi, North Kivu, Maniema and Kongo-Central but gives ambiguous site mapping.

demand.evidence: 13 months of salary arrears despite prior agreement.

state_target.evidence: The demand concerns employees of a public agency and an agreement involving the supervising Minister; source also criticizes agency authorities.

attendance_simultaneous.evidence: No site-level count. Multi-site action is not converted to one national total.

notes: One low-detail outlet/body; the geographical phrasing is internally imprecise. An independent source and site-specific attendance evidence remain gaps.
open_questions: What was simultaneous attendance at each ANADEC site, without combining separate locations?
Can precise locations and independent corroboration be established from available reporting?

title: Reported NOGEC pro-constitutional-reform meeting in Tshangu
location: Tshangu, Kinshasa; exact site in captured FNTV result not specified
organizer: NOGEC / Constant Mutamba, described as a party led by a government minister
summary: A search-result headline says Mutamba addressed a large crowd on 14 Dec; FNTV body was inaccessible through the tool and Ecomine follow-up body returned HTTP 403. Opinion Info body only describes meetings in future tense and does not confirm this event. No crowd count can be taken from “marée humaine.”

occurrence.evidence: FNTV’s captured search header claims an actual 14 Dec crowd; no article body available. Ecomine search header is a Dec 16 follow-up but body denied.

date.evidence: FNTV headline dates the report/event 14 December; Ecomine result dated 16 December.

location.evidence: Tshangu appears in both headlines, exact meeting place not established by body.

demand.evidence: Search headlines concern constitutional reform, but available body only confirms a future plan in Opinion Info.

state_target.evidence: Search-result descriptions connect the meeting to constitutional reform and a government minister; direct body support pending.

attendance_simultaneous.evidence: FNTV headline uses “marée humaine,” a non-quantified rhetorical description; no count or body.

notes: No claim of inclusion. FNTV open failed with a tool-level no-access message and no HTTP status; Ecomine returned actual HTTP 403 and was not retried. Independent confirmation and precise attendance are needed. Opinion Info article says the planned meetings “will” happen and is not execution evidence.
open_questions: Did the announced 14 December Tshangu pro-change meeting actually occur, and what body evidence identifies its site and state-policy demand?
Is there any reliable body-level evidence of simultaneous attendance meeting the threshold, and did the separately announced opposition meeting occur?
